facts.value: Primary emergency rescue, fire suppression, and search-and-rescue operations across Lebanon. Also provides guidance on earthquake preparedness, explosion aftermath, and flood/disaster response.
Emergency medical services (EMS) and pre-hospital patient transport.

First responder for: structural collapses, cracking or collapsing building walls, sinkhole emergencies, flood rescues, fire incidents, person trapped, exposed live electrical cables, explosion scenes, maritime/coastal emergencies.
Emergency hotline: 125. Call immediately for any life-safety incident. 125 is the ONLY correct Civil Defense emergency number — 175 is incorrect.
facts.notes: 125 confirmed prominently on civildefense.gov.lb homepage and contact page on 2026-05-31. Previous internal draft erroneously used 175 — VERIFIED: correct number is 125.

facts.value: Emergency dispatch: immediate (within minutes of 125 call). No published SLA — operational standard is fastest possible response. Non-emergency complaints via complaints@civildefense.gov.lb have no published response time.
facts.notes: No official published SLA. CedarFix operational classification: immediate emergency.

facts.value: For life-safety emergencies: call 125 immediately — this must always be the first action. For non-emergency complaints about Civil Defense conduct or service: email complaints@civildefense.gov.lb or call/fax 01/287125. Alternatively use the online contact form at civildefense.gov.lb/index.php?page=co. CedarFix must always trigger HITL when routing to Civil Defense and display number 125 prominently in the citizen-facing response.

150+ stations nationwide across all governorates (Beirut, Mount Lebanon, North, Akkar, Baalbek-Hermel, Bekaa, South, Nabatiyeh). Stations operate in 4 capability tiers: (1) Land Fire Fighting only, (2) Land Fire Fighting + Ambulance (most common), (3) Sea Rescue Unit, (4) Sea Rescue Unit + Ambulance. Confirmed sea rescue station locations: Tyre Marine Station (South — Sea Rescue + Ambulance), Jounieh Kaslik (Mount Lebanon — Sea Rescue + Ambulance), Al Abde (North coast — Sea Rescue). For maritime emergencies, route to the nearest sea rescue station. Station coverage is dense enough that virtually every Lebanese caza has at least one CD station. Note: station map data sourced from April 2010 — some stations may have opened or closed since.
facts.notes: Extracted from official Lebanese Civil Defense stations map PDF (prepared by M.S., dated 1.04.2010). Sea rescue stations confirmed at Tyre, Jounieh/Kaslik, Al Abde. Medium confidence due to 2010 date — verify current station list via civildefense.gov.lb المراكز section.

primary_for_sectors: EMERGENCY_rescue — person trapped, buried, or missing
EMERGENCY_structural — building collapse, cracking walls, imminent structural failure
EMERGENCY_flood — active flood rescue (not drain blockage)
ELECTRICITY_downed — exposed or downed live electrical cables (always co-notified with EDL)
secondary_for_sectors: ROADS_sinkhole — sinkhole with risk to persons
FLOODING_non_emergency — co-notified with municipality for severe weather flooding
not_responsible_for: Non-emergency infrastructure complaints — route to MUN, EDL, MPWT, or water establishments
Crime or public order — route to ISF
Routine electrical outages with no life-safety risk — route to EDL
Drain blockages with no rescue risk — route to MUN
hitl_conditions: Any incident classified as life-safety emergency — always show 125 prominently
Exposed or downed live electrical cables — co-notify EDL simultaneously
